title: Incremental traffic evacuation protocol for cross-region node degradation
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Draft and validate an incremental traffic evacuation and drain protocol that operators can execute during partial or progressive cross-region degradation affecting both Hosted and Dedicated customers. Current failover procedures are blunt (full-region cutovers) and cause unnecessary cold-cache and spike costs for Dedicated tenants pinned to specific regions. This ticket creates a stepwise runbook, automated helpers, and verification gates to shift traffic in small increments (5-25%) with KV cache warm-up and performance gating to minimize error rates and customer-visible slowdowns.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook reviewed by SRE, Runtime, and Console teams and approved in a 1-hour tabletop
Automation script to shift traffic by N% validated in staging with synthetic traffic and observability hooks
KV cache warmup hook exists and can be toggled per-customer group
Latency and error gating thresholds implemented and can abort shift automatically
Post-shift verification checklist with dashboards and alerting playbooks documented
One customer-facing dry-run performed with a non-critical Dedicated tenant and results logged
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: confirm region degradation signature (e.g., GPU OOMs, scheduler backlog, control-plane timeouts). Attach incident ticket and affected zones.
2) Scope: enumerate impacted customers and mark Dedicated tenants with region affinity. Classify by SLAs and active sessions.
3) Prepare: open coordination Slack channel (#inc-evac-ENG-<region>), notify on-call SRE and account owner for impacted Dedicated customers.
4) Warmup cache: enable KV prefetch for target model variants and initiate prefix cache warmup against a warmup worker pool. Verify average cache hit rate increases.
5) Incremental shift: use traffic-shift automation to move 5% of traffic to fallback region; wait 60s baseline, check p50/p95 latency and 5xx rate.
6) Gate evaluation: if latency increase >15% or 5xx rate >0.5% above baseline, abort and roll back to previous distribution; file follow-up investigation.
7) Continue ramp: on success, step to 15%, 30%, then 50% with checks after each step and increased observation windows for Dedicated tenants with session affinity.
8) Post-evac validation: run consistency checks for responses, KV sync integrity, and sampling-based quality evaluation (prompt-set regressions).
9) Customer comms: coordinate with Support to post status updates and affected-tenant advisory notes; offer dedicated capacity credits if SLA breach likely.
10) Close: capture metrics (token costs, extra infra hours, error counts), create incident postmortem link, and list follow-up engineering tasks.
rollback_plan: If any gate trips or a Dedicated tenant reports session loss or consistent quality regressions, immediately run the automation to revert traffic distribution to the last known-good snapshot. If revert fails due to control-plane instability, escalate to SRE and trigger emergency full-region redirect with immediate customer notifications. After rollback, preserve logs and KV cache snapshots for forensics.
qa_plan: Staging exercise with synthetic workloads and at least two model families (decoder-only and encoder-decoder).
End-to-end trace verification for 10 sample requests per shifted percentage to confirm KV cache warmup efficacy.
Chaos test: simulate delayed control plane responses during a 15% shift and verify automated abort behavior.
Run a Canary with a volunteer Dedicated tenant in a non-production org and gather SLO metrics for 24 hours.
